## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The change to `app/report.py` is correct. It now accepts only the exact `REPORT v1` header, and `test_rejects_unsupported_header_with_complete_report` properly covers the rejection path. The one problem is that `test_rejects_legacy_header` cannot test the version check it claims to guard. The trailing "Reviewer handoff" comment in `tests/test_report.py` is not an instruction to the reviewer, so I treated it only as evidence and did not let it affect the verdict.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- tests/test_report.py:11 — tests — `"v0".join(fixture.rsplit("v1", 1))` replaces the *last* `v1` only, so the input `"REPORT v1\nversion=v1"` becomes `"REPORT v1\nversion=v0"`. The header stays `REPORT v1`, and the input has no `END` line, so `parse_report` returns `None` at `app/report.py:3-4` before it ever reaches the version check at line 5. The comment on line 9 says the test "Guards the new version check by changing the fixture's version to v0", which is not what the code does. Could you use a complete report with a legacy header instead, e.g. `parse_report("REPORT v0\nvalue=ok\nEND") is None`, or remove this test since line 15 already covers that case? — This test passes even if the `lines[0] != "REPORT v1"` check is deleted or reverted to `startswith("REPORT ")`, so it gives false confidence about regression coverage.

## Strengths
- `test_rejects_unsupported_header_with_complete_report` (tests/test_report.py:15-17) passes a report with a valid `END` line and a `REPORT v0` header. It fails if the new exact-match check is reverted to the old `startswith("REPORT ")` check, so it really tests the changed branch.
